page: Microsoft Azure D8as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture, clocked at 3.525 GHz. It provides 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and AVX instruction sets.

The server does not include a dedicated GPU accelerator, relying entirely on the central processor for computational workloads. Bundled storage is limited to a 69 GB local SSD, intended primarily for temporary files, swap space, or caching rather than persistent enterprise databases. Network provisioning does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires explicit assignment of networking resources if external connectivity is necessary.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across varied computational tasks. Single-core execution is solid, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 2,706.97 in the top 25% bracket and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,603.0. Multi-core performance aligns broadly within average ranges, recording 10,823.73 in stress-ng and 6,487.0 in Geekbench multi-core. PassMark metrics indicate balanced compute (11,910.93) and memory (2,573.92) throughput. Memory bandwidth ranges from 515.21 GB/sec for small cached blocks down to 52.74 GB/sec read and 32.12 GB/sec write for uncached transfers. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression stands out as an area of weaker throughput at 35.43 GB/sec.

With its balanced allocation of 8 vCPUs and 32 GB RAM, the D8as_v4 represents a cost-efficient resource tier for workloads that do not demand extensive storage or dedicated graphics processing. It is technically suited for static web serving, enterprise application hosting, microservices, Clang-based software compilation, and moderate in-memory key-value stores like Redis, achieving over 8.2 million set operations per second.

It is provisioned with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), and 69 GB of bundled local SSD temporary storage without an integrated GPU. Architectural features include 32 MB of L3 cache, AVX extensions, and hardware cryptographic instructions. Benchmarks show strong single-core performance alongside balanced mid-range multi-core scores, verified by a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,487.0 and Redis throughput exceeding 8.2 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers at 52.74 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 32.12 GB/sec for writes. The instance offers a balanced hardware profile for web serving, microservices, application backends, and software compilation.
